chunks: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from a man of the Banu Hashim, who said:

I heard him say: 'Four [traits] are such that whoever possesses them, his Islam is complete, even if what is between his horns and his feet [i.e., his whole body] is covered in sins, that will not diminish it: Truthfulness, Modesty, Good Character, and Gratitude.'
ai.seo_question: What four traits complete a person's Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Attributed to the Prophet Muhammad via a Hashimi narrator, this hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* emphasizes that truthfulness (al-Sidq), modesty (al-Haya), good character (Husn al-Khuluq), and gratitude (al-Shukr) are the pillars that perfect one's faith. In Shia scholarly tradition, these traits are viewed not merely as moral virtues but as essential spiritual anchors that preserve the integrity of Islam, ensuring that even if other sins are committed, the core of one's faith remains intact and undiminished.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 4.Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from a man of the Banī Hāshim saying,

“I heard him say, ‘Four traits are such that whoever possesses them, his submission [to Allah] is complete, even if he is covered in misdeeds from head to toe. They are: truthfulness, modesty, good character, and gratitude.’”
